name: Larkspur
lore: Larkspur is a hillside market town about two hours' walk east of Riverton, built of honey-coloured stone around hot springs. It lives on wool, dye and visitors who come for the baths; its folk are cheerful, fond of gossip and festivals, and quick to overcharge anyone from the river.

west_road.name: West Road
west_road.lore: The road between Larkspur and Riverton winds through sheep pasture and over a stone bridge; it's about a two-hour walk.

road.name: West Road
road.description: A dusty road climbing out of the sheep pastures toward Larkspur's honey-coloured roofs. A stone bridge crosses a beck, and a signpost points west: Riverton, two hours on foot.

exits.description: The long road west winds away through farmland until it drops out of sight. Riverton is about two hours' walk.
Up the hill into Larkspur.

green.name: Larkspur Streets
green.lore: Steep stone streets hung with dyed wool drying on lines, steaming gutters fed by the springs, and the smell of sulphur and lavender.

green.name: Larkspur Green
green.description: A sloping village green around a steaming spring-fed fountain. A maypole stands at the top, washing lines of brightly dyed wool flap overhead, and streets climb toward the baths and wind down toward the dyeworks.

exits.description: Down the hill to the West Road and, two hours on, Riverton.
Worn stone steps climb toward the bathhouse.
A steep cobbled street winds down past the dyeworks.
The painted doors of the Larkspur Playhouse.

bath_steps.name: Bathhouse Steps
bath_steps.description: A terrace of worn stone steps, slick with mineral steam. The columned front of the Larkspur Baths rises at the top, and a small herb shop with a green door sits halfway up.

exits.description: Down the steps to the green.
The bronze-studded doors of the Larkspur Baths.
The green door of Wren's Apothecary, standing open to let the herb smell out.

weavers_row.name: Weavers Row
weavers_row.description: A steep street of narrow houses with looms clacking behind open shutters. The gutters run blue, red and yellow from the dyeworks at the bottom, and a bookbinder's bow window glows with lamplight.

exits.description: Up the hill to the green.
The wide gate of the dyeworks yard.
The bookbinder's door, under a swinging sign shaped like an open book.

baths.name: The Larkspur Baths
baths.lore: The town's pride: hot mineral baths run by Odessa Vey, a tall, statuesque bath-mistress with dark curls pinned up, a towel over one bare shoulder and a warm, unhurried voice. Her attendants are lithe, cheerful girls in linen shifts.

hall.name: Entrance Hall
hall.description: A cool marble hall with a mosaic of leaping fish on the floor. Folded towels are stacked on shelves, and a pretty attendant takes coins at a desk beside a curtained archway.

exits.description: The bronze-studded doors onto the Bathhouse Steps.
Through the curtained archway to the baths.

pool.name: Great Pool
pool.description: A vaulted hall around a wide, steaming green pool fed by a spring that bubbles up from the rock. Light falls through a glass dome, and stone benches line the edges.

exits.description: The curtained archway back to the entrance hall.
A heavy oak door, beaded with moisture.
A plain door marked for staff only.

steam_room.name: Steam Room
steam_room.description: A small, dim, tiled room so thick with herb-scented steam that faces blur at arm's length. Water hisses on hot stones in a copper brazier.

exits.description: The heavy oak door back to the Great Pool.

boiler.name: Boiler Room
boiler.description: A hot, cramped room of pipes, valves and a great copper tank that groans as spring water is pumped through it. Coal dust and steam hang in the air.

exits.description: The staff door back to the Great Pool.
A rusted grate low in the wall, where warm air whistles through from somewhere beyond.
exits.traversal: Past the loose grate is a cramped duct, hot and black with soot; it is a slow belly-crawl toward the cooler air and the smell of greasepaint.

apothecary.name: Wren's Apothecary
apothecary.lore: A herb shop run by Wren, a petite, freckled redhead with ink-stained fingers and a mischievous smile, who sells remedies, perfumes and, to the right people, stronger things.

shop.name: Wren's Apothecary
shop.description: A narrow shop crowded with labelled jars, bundles of lavender and a brass scale on the counter. The air is sweet and bitter at once, and a ladder leads up through a hatch.

exits.description: The green door onto the Bathhouse Steps.
A ladder up through a hatch.

loft.name: Drying Loft
loft.description: A low attic under the roof beams, hung with drying herbs and flowers. A small window looks out over the steaming roofs of the baths.

exits.description: The ladder back down to the shop.

dyeworks.name: Hollin Dyeworks
dyeworks.lore: The dyeworks that colour Larkspur's wool, run by Maren Hollin, a strong, sun-browned woman with blue-stained forearms, a bold laugh and a kerchief over her black hair, with a crew of brawny, good-humoured dye-girls.

yard.name: Dyeworks Yard
yard.description: A busy yard of steaming vats in blue, crimson and saffron. Skeins of wool hang from poles, the ground is stained every colour, and the air stinks of woad and boiling madder root.

exits.description: The wide gate onto Weavers Row.
A barn door into the storehouse.

storehouse.name: Storehouse
storehouse.description: A dim barn piled high with bales of raw wool, sacks of dried roots and barrels of alum. Finished bolts of dyed cloth are stacked in neat, bright towers.

exits.description: The barn door back to the yard.

bindery.name: Sable's Bindery
bindery.lore: A bookbinder and scribe's shop run by Sable, a slim, elegant woman with silver-streaked hair in a long braid, reading spectacles and a dry wit, who also writes letters for those who can't.

shop.name: Sable's Bindery
shop.description: A quiet shop smelling of leather and glue, with presses, racks of paper and a writing desk in the bow window. Shelves of bound books line every wall.

exits.description: The door onto Weavers Row.

playhouse.name: The Larkspur Playhouse
playhouse.lore: A small, gaudy playhouse that puts on comedies and festival masques, run by Celandine Rook, a glamorous, full-figured actress-manager with a husky voice and a fondness for scandal. Her troupe of actresses is young, pretty and always short of money.

foyer.name: Foyer
foyer.description: A small foyer papered with playbills, with a ticket window, faded red curtains and a painted ceiling of cherubs. Doors lead through to the auditorium.

exits.description: The painted doors onto Larkspur Green.
Through to the auditorium.

auditorium.name: Auditorium
auditorium.description: Rows of worn benches face a raised stage framed in gilt plaster. Painted backdrops of castles and forests hang above, and candles in tin footlights line the stage edge.

exits.description: Back to the foyer.
A narrow door beside the stage.
A trapdoor in the stage boards, used for ghosts and demons.
exits.traversal: The trapdoor drops onto a short ladder; it is a quick, creaking climb down into the dusty dark under the stage.

dressing_rooms.name: Dressing Rooms
dressing_rooms.description: A cramped warren of mirrors, costume racks and pots of greasepaint, littered with wigs, fans and love letters.

exits.description: The narrow door back to the stage.

under_stage.name: Under the Stage
under_stage.description: A low, dusty space beneath the stage boards, full of old props, ropes and pulleys. Warm air drifts from somewhere in the dark.

exits.description: A ladder up to the trapdoor in the stage.
exits.traversal: A creaking climb up the ladder; the trapdoor heaves up and the stage boards are underfoot.

exits.description: A rusted grate behind a stack of painted flats, warm and smelling of steam.
exits.traversal: Behind the grate a soot-black duct runs on and on; it is a slow, sweltering belly-crawl toward the hiss of steam.
